description: How IT is run as a set of services that create value and how it is directed and controlled: service value and the service value system, the service desk, incident, problem, change and release management, service level agreements, IT governance frameworks, risk, audit and compliance, and measuring IT performance. Students work tickets, changes and outages on a simulated IT department in the browser, write service level agreements and run a governance and audit review against recognised frameworks.
modelledOn: AXELOS, ITIL 4 Foundation and the ITIL 4 practice guides
ISACA, COBIT 2019 Framework: Governance and Management Objectives
ISO/IEC 38500, Governance of IT for the organisation
outcomes: Explain how IT services co-create value and describe the service value system, value chain and guiding principles.
Operate service desk, incident, request and problem management processes and prioritise work by impact and urgency.
Plan and assess changes and releases so that risk to live services is controlled.
Negotiate and write service level agreements with measurable targets and supporting agreements.
Apply IT governance, risk and audit frameworks to evaluate controls and compliance in an organisation.
Design metrics, dashboards and improvement plans that measure IT performance against business goals.

units.title: IT services and value
topics: Services, products, service offerings and service relationships; value co-creation with consumers
Utility and warranty; outcomes, costs and risks
The four dimensions of service management: organisations and people, information and technology, partners and suppliers, value streams and processes
IT as a cost centre versus a service provider; services at a university, a bank and a mobile operator

units.title: The service value system
topics: The service value system: guiding principles, governance, the service value chain, practices and continual improvement
The seven guiding principles and how they shape decisions
Service value chain activities: plan, improve, engage, design and transition, obtain or build, deliver and support
Service catalogue and service portfolio management; mapping a value stream

units.title: Service desk, incidents and requests
topics: Service desk structures: local, centralised, virtual and follow-the-sun; channels including phone, WhatsApp and SMS
Incident lifecycle: logging, categorisation, prioritisation by impact and urgency, diagnosis, escalation and closure
Major incident procedures and communication during outages
Service requests and request fulfilment; self-service portals and knowledge bases
Ticketing tools, queues and workload; first-contact resolution
Handling a mobile money outage on a public holiday

units.title: Problem management
topics: Problems, known errors and workarounds; reactive and proactive problem management
Root cause analysis techniques: five whys, Ishikawa diagrams, fault tree and Kepner-Tregoe analysis
Trend analysis of incident data to find recurring problems
Blameless post-incident reviews

units.title: Change and release management
topics: Change enablement: standard, normal and emergency changes; change authority and the change advisory board
Risk and impact assessment, change schedules and freeze periods
Release and deployment management: release planning, build, test, deployment and early life support
Configuration management: configuration items, the CMDB and service dependency maps
Integrating change management with DevOps, continuous delivery and automated testing
Planning a core banking upgrade with minimal downtime

units.title: Service levels and agreements
topics: Service level management: service level requirements, targets and reviews
Service level agreements, operational level agreements and underpinning contracts
Availability, capacity, continuity and information security as warranty requirements
Supplier and relationship management; SLAs with internet and cloud providers serving low-bandwidth regions
Writing an SLA with measurable availability and response targets

units.title: IT governance frameworks
topics: Corporate governance and IT governance; governance versus management
COBIT 2019: governance system principles, objectives, components, design factors and capability levels
ISO/IEC 38500 principles: evaluate, direct and monitor
ISO/IEC 20000 certification and how ITIL, COBIT and ISO standards fit together
IT strategy, investment decisions, IT steering committees and portfolio governance
Governance of public sector IT and e-government services in Ghana

units.title: Risk, audit and compliance
topics: IT risk management: identification, assessment, risk appetite, treatment and risk registers
Internal controls: preventive, detective and corrective; general and application controls
The IT audit process: planning, evidence, testing controls and reporting findings
Compliance obligations: ISO/IEC 27001, data protection law and sector regulators such as the Bank of Ghana
Business continuity and disaster recovery planning; recovery time and recovery point objectives

units.title: Measuring IT performance
topics: Critical success factors, KPIs and metrics; the metrics hierarchy from operational to strategic
Service metrics: availability, MTTR, MTBF, first-contact resolution and customer satisfaction
IT balanced scorecard and value measurement; cost of services and chargeback
Continual improvement models and maturity assessment
Service reporting dashboards for management

units.title: Capstone
topics: Assessing the service management maturity of a simulated organisation
Running a governance and audit review against COBIT objectives
Producing a service improvement plan with prioritised actions and metrics
Presenting findings to an IT steering committee

schedule.title: Services, value and the four dimensions
schedule.exercise: Choose a service at a bank, a university and a mobile operator and, for each, write its utility, its warranty and one cost and risk it carries.

tasks.title: Decide whether a described IT offering has acceptable utility and warranty for a given customer, and name the missing element if it fails
Map a described outage across the four dimensions of service management and decide which dimension most needs attention to prevent recurrence
Argue, for a university IT department, whether it should operate as a cost centre or a service provider, and defend the choice against a counter-argument

schedule.title: The service value system
schedule.exercise: Pick two of the seven guiding principles and show, with a short example, how each would change a real IT decision.

tasks.title: Apply two guiding principles to resolve a described conflict between a quick fix and a proper solution, and justify the chosen path
Map a described value stream (from a request to a delivered service) onto the service value chain activities, and name any activity that was skipped
Design a service catalogue entry for a described IT offering, including what is in and out of scope, and spot a catalogue gap in a client's current list

schedule.title: Service desk and incident management
schedule.exercise: Write the first three questions a service desk agent should ask for an incident report, and explain how they set impact and urgency.

tasks.title: Log, categorise and prioritise five incoming incident reports by impact and urgency, and decide which should escalate immediately
Choose the best service desk structure (local, centralised, virtual, follow-the-sun) for a described multi-branch bank, with reasons
Run the communication plan for a major incident during a service outage, deciding what to tell customers, staff and management and when

schedule.title: Request fulfilment and handling an outage
schedule.exercise: Design a self-service portal menu for three common requests at a mobile operator, and explain how each cuts load on the service desk.

tasks.title: Design a self-service request flow and a knowledge base entry for a common request, and estimate the first-contact resolution it would enable
Triage a queue of mixed incidents and requests by priority and route each to the right team, explaining any reordering from arrival order
Handle a mobile money service outage reported on a public holiday, deciding who to call, what to communicate and in what order, scored on a rubric

schedule.title: Problem management
schedule.exercise: Perform a five-whys analysis on a recurring service failure of your choosing and state the root cause the first why would have missed.

tasks.title: Build an Ishikawa diagram for a recurring service failure, sorting likely causes into categories, and identify the most probable root cause
Decide whether three described situations are incidents, problems or known errors, and choose the matching workaround or fix for each
Run a blameless post-incident review for a described failure, separating contributing factors from blame and producing two concrete follow-up actions

schedule.title: Change, release and configuration management
schedule.exercise: Classify five proposed IT changes as standard, normal or emergency, and explain what approval each would need before going ahead.

tasks.title: Classify five proposed changes as standard, normal or emergency, route each to the right approval, and flag one that was miscategorised
Assess the risk and impact of a proposed change and decide whether it can proceed inside a stated freeze period, with reasons
Plan a core banking system upgrade with minimal downtime, sequencing change approval, release steps and a rollback point, scored on a rubric

schedule.title: Configuration management and DevOps integration
schedule.exercise: Sketch a configuration item dependency map for a simple three-tier application and explain which change would be riskiest to make.

tasks.title: Draw a configuration management database dependency map for a described application stack and mark the single point of failure
Decide how a change advisory board process should adapt for a team doing frequent automated deployments, without losing proper oversight
Plan a release through build, test, deployment and early life support for a described update, and name the gate that would have caught a described defect

schedule.title: Service level management
schedule.exercise: Write a service level agreement clause with a measurable availability target and a response time target for an internet connectivity service.

tasks.title: Draft an SLA and a matching operational level agreement for a described internal service, checking the targets are consistent with each other
Evaluate a proposed SLA from an internet provider serving a low-bandwidth region, flagging any target that looks unrealistic for the stated conditions
Write an SLA with a measurable availability target and response time for a stated service, and justify the numbers against the business need

schedule.title: Corporate and IT governance
schedule.exercise: Explain, with an example, the difference between governance and management, and where the boundary sits in a described decision.

tasks.title: Decide whether five described activities are governance or management, and justify any that are harder to classify
Apply a COBIT 2019 governance objective to a described weakness and name the component (process, structure or policy) most in need of change
Evaluate a described IT decision against the ISO/IEC 38500 evaluate, direct and monitor cycle, and identify which stage was skipped

schedule.title: Standards, strategy and e-government
schedule.exercise: Write a short note comparing what ITIL, COBIT and ISO/IEC 20000 each contribute to running IT well, and where they overlap.

tasks.title: Map a described organisation's current practices against ITIL, COBIT and ISO/IEC 20000 and recommend which standard to formalise first
Prioritise three competing IT investment proposals for a steering committee using a described portfolio governance method
Assess the governance of a described public e-government service in Ghana and recommend one accountability improvement

schedule.title: Risk, controls and audit
schedule.exercise: Build a risk register entry for one IT risk you consider likely at a Ghanaian bank, with likelihood, impact, treatment and an owner.

tasks.title: Identify, assess and propose a treatment for three IT risks in a described organisation, and place each on a risk register
Decide whether a described control is preventive, detective or corrective, and recommend a missing control for a described gap
Plan an IT audit for a described system, including evidence to collect and tests of controls, and draft one finding

schedule.title: Metrics, scorecards and improvement
schedule.exercise: Design a one-page service reporting dashboard for management showing three metrics from the operational level up to the strategic level.

tasks.title: Choose three critical success factors for a described IT department and the KPI that would show progress on each, from the operational up to the strategic level
Choose the right metric (availability, MTTR, MTBF, first-contact resolution, satisfaction) to diagnose three described service complaints
Assess a described organisation's continual improvement maturity and recommend the single highest-value next step, supported by two metrics from its scorecard

schedule.title: Maturity assessment and the governance capstone
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page service improvement plan for a simulated organisation, naming its three weakest practices, a prioritised action for each and the metric that would show improvement.

tasks.title: Assess the service management maturity of a simulated organisation against a described maturity model and justify the level assigned
Produce a service improvement plan with three prioritised actions and the metric that would show each has worked
Run a governance and audit review of a simulated organisation against COBIT objectives, producing a prioritised improvement plan and a summary for a steering committee, scored on a capstone rubric
